summary: Discovery call for Dedicated capacity. Lakeland Bank is evaluating Redwood Dedicated vs hosted and private options to support a customer-facing virtual assistant and fraud-detection batch jobs. Key topics: isolation needs, burst strategy, autoscale policies, latency vs cost tradeoffs, security/compliance (SOC2, KMS), and benchmark plan. Next step is pricing, security pack, and a technical deep-dive + benchmark.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-01T15:00:00-05:00
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Lakeland Head of AI), Priya Nair (Lakeland Infrastructure), Carlos Martinez (Lakeland Security)

Summary: quick discovery about dedicated capacity needs, isolation, burst capacity and scaling.

[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, with Samir our solutions engineer, how's it going?
[00:00:07] Jordan: Good thanks, appreciate you all. We wanted to go through our requirements for a dedicated deployment.
[00:00:12] Maya: Great. Real quick can you give us the high level use cases and expected qps / latency targets?
[00:00:19] Jordan: Sure, two main workloads. One is a customer-facing chat assistant, expected peak 120 requests per second, average 40, target p95 latency under 400ms for short dialogs. Second is nightly batch scoring for fraud models — that's heavy throughput but can be scheduled. Also we want data isolation, cannot send customer PII to shared tenants.
[00:00:40] Priya: To add, we have strong network controls, we want VPC peering, private subnets, and key management via our HSM. SOC 2 is required.
[00:00:48] Samir: Okay makes sense. For Dedicated we typically reserve GPU pools. Do you have an idea of model size and token rates per request?
[00:00:56] Jordan: We're looking at a 13B to 33B family for the assistant, about 150 tokens per request on average. Batch scoring uses a smaller embedder model but high volume.
[00:01:06] Maya: Good — that helps sizing. For 120 rps at ~150 tokens, continuous throughput could be substantial; we usually size by sustained qps and then define burst capacity. Do you expect simultaneous spikes above 120?
[00:01:17] Jordan: We have marketing spikes — up to 2x for short windows, maybe 5-10 minutes. So burst policy is important.
[00:01:24] Samir: We support burst with reserved headroom and burst queues. There are two patterns: reserve enough GPUs for sustained load and configure short-term burst using excess capacity or cloud-backed autoscaling. For strict isolation you can opt for dedicated-only GPUs which prevents noisy neighbors but increases cost.
[00:01:40] Carlos: On isolation — we need guaranteed no co-tenancy with other customers. Also audit logs of all requests and ability to retain logs for 13 months.
[00:01:48] Maya: Absolutely. Dedicated gives you isolated pools and you can enable audit logging and long-term retention. We also integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping.
[00:01:56] Priya: For networking, we need egress restrictions and only private endpoints, not internet-facing. Can Redwood Private be an option?
[00:02:03] Maya: Redwood Private is an option (VPC/on-prem). Dedicated can also be deployed into your VPC with private endpoints. There's a tradeoff: Private gives more control but adds setup time and operational responsibilities.
[00:02:13] Jordan: What's the typical lead time for Dedicated vs Private?
[00:02:16] Samir: Dedicated into a Redwood-managed region with VPC peering usually 2-4 weeks after contract and infra review. Private on-prem or customer-managed control plane can be 6-12 weeks depending on approvals.
[00:02:28] Jordan: Ok that's helpful. Cost is a concern though — can we autoscale down for nights?
[00:02:33] Samir: Yes, we support scale-to-zero for non-critical pools and scheduled scaling for batch jobs. For strict reserved contracts you commit to baseline capacity but can add burst or overage billing.
[00:02:44] Jordan: About latency — we need p95 under 400ms. What tuning levers are available?
[00:02:49] Samir: Several: model choice (smaller/optimized models), quantization, kernel selection, batching strategy. Our runtime supports continuous batching, KV cache for conversations, and optimized kernels for attention. We can also suggest a quantization profile.
[00:03:04] Priya: A lot of our infra team uses Kubernetes. Do you require any agents or do you expose endpoint APIs?
[00:03:09] Maya: For Dedicated you get a managed GPU pool and API endpoints. For Private on-prem we provide a deployment package that you run in your environment; it can integrate with k8s.
[00:03:17] Carlos: Security questions: SAML SSO, RBAC, encryption at rest, audit trails — do you have a SOC 2 report?
[00:03:24] Maya: Yes we have SOC 2 and ISO attestations. We'll share the security pack. We also support customer-managed KMS, HSM integration, and fine-grained RBAC.
[00:03:33] Jordan: For the benchmark, we'd like to run a 48-hour test simulating our traffic patterns. Can Redwood help run that or provide a harness?
[00:03:40] Samir: Yes we can run benchmarks with your sample prompts, or give you a test harness. Typically we recommend starting with 24-48 hour runs to capture tails. We'll coordinate on the exact test plan.
[00:03:51] Jordan: If we go Dedicated and later want to move to Private, is that possible?
[00:03:54] Maya: Yes, we support migration paths. The APIs and config are consistent across modes; there may be data movement and infra changes but functionally it's supported.
[00:04:02] Priya: Regarding burst — you mentioned cloud-backed autoscaling. If we want strict isolation, can we still allow short bursts without co-tenancy?
[00:04:09] Samir: There are two options: keep a headroom buffer in your dedicated pool, or approve controlled bursts onto separate, reserved capacity that only your account can access. If absolute physical isolation is required, headroom is the safe choice.
[00:04:22] Carlos: What's the SLA on dedicated latency and uptime?
[00:04:25] Maya: For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime for the pool and per-request latency SLOs we jointly define. We'll include the SLA options in the pricing doc.
[00:04:33] Jordan: On observability we need per-route latency breakdowns and token-level cost reporting to feed into our chargeback.
[00:04:39] Samir: That's built into Redwood Console — token-level cost, per-model dashboards, traces, and alerting. You can export metrics to your monitoring stack.
[00:04:47] Maya: Quick note: sometimes the transcriptions call KV cache as K-V cash in decks, so apologies if any of the docs are fuzzy on terminology.
[00:04:53] Jordan: (laughs) we've seen that.
[00:04:56] Priya: Any regulatory restrictions we should flag? Data residency?
[00:04:59] Maya: We have region options for data residency and Dedicated pools can be provisioned in specific regions. For regulated workloads we recommend Private or Dedicated with strong network and KMS controls.
[00:05:10] Jordan: Great. Let's talk numbers — what would cost look like for baseline and burst?
[00:05:14] Maya: I'll send a pricing sheet with two scenarios: baseline reserved capacity sized for your sustained load and a second scenario with lower baseline + burst buffer or cloud-backed autoscale. Pricing will show committed monthly cost and overage rates.
[00:05:25] Jordan: Perfect.
[00:05:27] Samir: For the benchmark I'll need sample prompts, token distribution, and expected concurrency. Jordan can share that after the call.
[00:05:33] Jordan: I'll share a sample traffic export and security person will share the SOC requirements.
[00:05:38] Maya: Excellent. Recap: we'll send Dedicated pricing and SLA options, security pack (SOC2/ISO + network docs), and Samir will send a benchmark plan. We'll schedule the technical deep-dive next week.
[00:05:50] Carlos: Sounds good. One more Q on encryption in transit — do you support mTLS for internal endpoints?
[00:05:56] Samir: Yes we support mTLS and private endpoints.
[00:05:59] Jordan: Thanks everyone.
[00:06:01] Maya: Thanks team, we'll follow up in email with links to the docs and the pricing.

End of transcript. Note: transcription has occasional imperfect words and headers may be auto-gen.

References/Shared artifacts: Pricing deck (link sent after call), Security pack (SOC2/ISO) link to be shared, Benchmark plan (to be created by Samir).

Call ended at ~15:45 local time.
